fields.description:
## The defect

The `Git version floor gate` step added by ticket 980d-83ac-a6bb-4edb (merged as c433663721)
reads `.github/git-version-floor.txt` from the CHECKED-OUT PATCHSET TREE and errors when the
file is absent:

    ::error::missing <floorfile> (the single source of the Git version floor)

But the Gerrit `Verified` lane runs the WORKFLOW DEFINITION FROM `main`, not from the patchset
-- 980d documented this itself as a caveat about its own gate not self-testing. The two facts
combine badly:

  workflow (from main)     -> HAS the new gate step
  tree     (from patchset) -> may NOT have the floor file

Any change branched before 980d merged gets the gate but not its data file, and fails hard.

## Confirmed instance

Change 1416 (ticket fd30-a088-cbbc-4dbd): LLM-Review +1, Verified -1 from run 30978915944 with
4/4 pytest legs failing (ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13, macos py3.13). Verified directly:
`git ls-tree FETCH_HEAD .github/` on patchset 1 lists `module-size-limit.txt` but NOT
`git-version-floor.txt`. The change is unrelated to Git versions -- it edits the Makefile and
docs -- and its author had run the full suite green locally (10234 passed).

## Blast radius

Every open change branched before c433663721 merged. At filing there were 6 open changes;
1408/1410/1411 already carry Verified +1 from runs that PREDATE the gate, so those green votes
no longer reflect what a re-run would produce -- a `recheck` on any of them should be expected
to flip to -1.

Same shape as bug 3787-9749-f8a6-41bb ("Rebase-If-Necessary submits a tree CI never
validated"): a mismatch between the tree CI evaluates and the tree that will land. Worth
considering whether the two share a fix.

## Candidate resolutions (weigh these; not prescribed)

1. Treat an absent floor file as "no floor declared" and PASS, so the gate enforces only once
   the file exists in the tree under test -- fail-open on absence, fail-closed on an actual
   under-floor git. Cheapest, and self-heals as changes rebase.
2. Read the floor from the workflow's own checkout so the gate's data travels with the gate.
3. Accept it and require every in-flight change to rebase -- viable, but it silently taxes
   every author and the message does not name rebasing as the remedy.

Whichever is chosen, the diagnostic must name the actual cause. "missing <floorfile>" sends an
author hunting for a file they never touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A change branched BEFORE the gate landed, with no Git-version-related edits, passes CI
      without being rebased -- proven RED-first against the current gate.
- [x] A genuinely under-floor git still fails, with the diagnostic naming required version,
      installed version and upgrade path (980d's behavior preserved, not weakened).
- [x] The missing-floor-file failure message names the real remedy, not just the filename.
- [x] Behavior is verified BOTH on a patchset tree lacking the file and one having it, since
      the workflow-from-main / tree-from-patchset split makes these different cases.

## Provenance

Found when change 1416 took an unexplained Verified -1 about an hour after 980d merged. 980d's
own report flagged that its gate "did not itself execute on this change ... it takes effect
from the next change onward" -- 1416 was that next change, and the effect was a false failure.


## Chosen fix (resolution 1, per the repo's own mandate)

Option 1 (treat an absent floor file as "no floor declared in this tree" and skip) is not
merely the cheapest -- it is the pattern this repository already MANDATES for exactly this
hazard. `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` documents the "Definition-vs-tree skew guard
(ticket ee2a)" and states verbatim:

    New gate steps that run a repo script must copy this if-present guard: skip (with a log
    line) when the script is absent from the checked-out tree; the gate re-enforces on rebase
    and on every post-merge change.

Two adjacent steps already implement it (`raw-git-write gate`, `wall-clock-assert gate`).
The Git-floor gate simply failed to copy it. So the fix is to apply the established
convention, keyed on `.github/git-version-floor.txt`, rather than invent a variant.

Option 2 (read the floor from the workflow's own checkout) is rejected: it would need a
second checkout of the target branch inside the gate step, diverging from the house pattern
for no benefit, and would make the gate enforce a floor the tree under test never declared.
Option 3 (require every author to rebase) is rejected: it taxes every in-flight change for a
defect they did not introduce.

### Design decisions

- DD1: replace the hard `exit 1` on a missing floor file with a skip that logs WHY it
  skipped -- naming the tree-skew cause and that the gate re-enforces on rebase / post-merge
  -- so the log names the real remedy instead of sending an author hunting for a file they
  never touched (AC 3).
- DD2: preserve 980d's enforcement verbatim for every OTHER path. When the floor file IS
  present, the parse, the comparison, and the under-floor diagnostic (required version,
  installed version, per-platform upgrade path) are unchanged (AC 2).
- DD3: leave `tests/conftest.py`'s `pytest_configure` session-abort and `tests/_git_floor.py`
  untouched -- the contributor-side floor enforcement is a separate consumer and is not
  weakened.
- DD4: prove the behavior by EXECUTING the real step. A new test extracts the `Git version
  floor gate` step's `run:` script from the workflow YAML and runs it under bash against
  three fixtures: a tree lacking the floor file (must exit 0 and log the skip reason), a tree
  having it (must enforce and pass on an adequate git), and a tree having it under a stubbed
  under-floor git (must exit 1 with the full diagnostic). This covers AC 4's requirement that
  BOTH tree cases be verified, since the workflow-from-main / tree-from-patchset split makes
  them genuinely different cases.

### Blast radius

One non-test file: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, one step. Plus one new test file.
No src/rebar change. The gate step is CI-only; the other floor consumers read the file
directly and are unaffected. The existing pins `test_ci_reads_the_floor_from_the_single_source`
and `test_consumers_declare_the_same_floor` continue to hold.
